strings.name: Hock Tan
strings.summary: Raised in Penang, Tan received a scholarship to study mechanical engineering at MIT, then earned a Harvard MBA. He moved from finance and industrial management into semiconductors and began leading Avago and its successor Broadcom in 2006. Acquisitions of chip companies, CA and VMware expanded the group into semiconductors and infrastructure software. His emphasis on costs and cash flow has also drawn customer controversy over software licensing and price changes.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; reviewed November 15, 2026. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Drove the integration of Broadcom’s semiconductor and infrastructure software businesses, influencing communications chips and the enterprise technology supply chain.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Penang, Malaysia; public sources support only 1951 or 1952 as his birth year, which remains unresolved.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: MIT bachelor’s and master’s degrees in mechanical engineering (1975); Harvard Business School MBA.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Spanning hardware and software
strings.highlights.h1.text: Led acquisitions and integration, extending Broadcom across communications chips and infrastructure software.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Combining engineering and management
strings.highlights.h2.text: Moved from mechanical engineering training into industrial finance and management, leading semiconductor businesses over many years.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Completing the VMware acquisition
strings.timeline.t1.text: Broadcom completed its VMware acquisition, expanding enterprise software and cloud infrastructure operations.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Acquiring CA Technologies
strings.timeline.t2.text: Broadcom completed its CA acquisition, extending beyond chips into enterprise software.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Combining Avago and Broadcom
strings.timeline.t3.text: Avago completed the Broadcom acquisition; the combined group adopted the Broadcom name.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Beginning to lead Avago
strings.timeline.t4.text: Became Avago president and CEO and continued to lead its successor Broadcom.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Leading Integrated Circuit Systems
strings.timeline.t5.text: Became the chip company’s president and CEO, serving until 2005.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Managing Pacven Investment
strings.timeline.t6.text: Became managing director of the Singapore investment fund, building on industrial and financial management experience.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Managing Hume Industries
strings.timeline.t7.text: Returned to Malaysia as an industrial company’s managing director after work at General Motors and PepsiCo.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completing MIT engineering degrees
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned bachelor’s and master’s degrees in mechanical engineering, later studying business administration at Harvard.
